clue.text: Specialist railway staff in age of steam? A seat I arranged with them

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of 'in age of steam' are shuffled, with those of 'A seat I' taken out of the pool

parts.note: the fodder: its letters are the answer's plus those of 'a seat I'
the letters removed from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look at the railwaymen of the steam era, with a seat being found for them.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'arranged' with 'with them' says the answer's letters plus A, S, E, A, T, I rearrange to make IN AGE OF STEAM. Fogmen laid detonators on the track as warnings in fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogmen were railway workers posted in foggy weather to place warning detonators on the line for drivers.

clue.text: Ordinary snake wriggling over old hedge in little wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first pieces above, i.e. before, what follows

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for ordinary (as in O level)

indicators.note: a wriggling snake twists about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
haw is an old word for a hedge or enclosure

explanation.surface: A grass snake slithers across an ancient hedgerow in a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggling' shuffles the snake into AKENS, and 'over' in a down clue puts O and AKENS above the hedge word; haw survives mainly in hawthorn, the hedging tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An oakenshaw is a small wood of oak trees, shaw being an old word for a thicket or copse.

clue.text: Investigator investigating manslaughter (characters implicated)

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a crime-novel aside, but in 'characters implicated' the characters are letters, folded into the words 'investigating manslaughter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-man is American slang for a federal agent of the FBI, a government investigator.

clue.text: He's master presenting e.g. Virgil

tuan is a Malay word for master or sir, used as a respectful title

explanation.surface: Someone praises a schoolmaster for presenting Virgil to the class.
explanation.walkthrough: TUAN, the Malay form of address meaning master or lord, is a well-worn crossword word in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was born near Mantua, so he is called the Mantuan; the term is a nickname by birthplace.

clue.text: Avoid or escape chop

parts.note: ESC is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: A choice between dodging the axe or fleeing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun it or keep clear of it deliberately, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Nest I had whenever in New York

explanation.definitionFit: To nidify is to build a nest, from Latin nidus; it is the verb sense of nest.

clue.text: Macbeth's upset well-informed actors in play

explanation.surface: Macbeth is rattled, and the well-briefed actors are on stage.

explanation.definitionFit: In Scots an upcast is an upset or reproach, so the Scottish usage matches upset.

clue.text: Haggle, getting penny change

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A haggler gets a penny back in change.
explanation.definitionFit: To palter is to haggle or bargain, and also to equivocate; Chambers gives both senses.

clue.text: Sound like birds in Scotland, Switzerland and Ireland

IRL is the international vehicle code for Ireland

explanation.surface: Birdsong is compared across Scotland, Switzerland and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Scotland' belongs to the definition: the answer is a Scots word, though it reads like the first of three countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirl is a Scots verb for warbling or chirping, the low trilling sound of a bird.

clue.text: It's dangerous removing hat that's jaunty

explanation.surface: A warning that taking off one's hat is risky, for a jaunty person.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can mean light-hearted and breezy, much as a jaunty manner is lively and carefree.

clue.text: Trespass in gran's mobile, breaking lock

clue.text: Irregular projection, for instance seen in edible bulb

as can introduce an example, as in 'trees, as oaks'

explanation.definitionFit: The camas is a North American plant of the lily family whose bulb was a staple food of Native peoples.

clue.text: Motor restricting undue speed no longer, report revealed

clue.text: E.g. TMS exhibits a team of troupers

parts.note: to sport something is to show it off, as in sporting a new hat
a cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A trademarked brand puts on a show featuring a troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: TMS is BBC radio's Test Match Special, its ball-by-ball cricket commentary; it looks like trademarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Test Match Special is a broadcast of sport, an example of a sportscast.

clue.text: Feverish states backward sloth annoyed

riled means annoyed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reads AI then RILED from the end, giving DELIR then IA. AI, the three-toed sloth, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is the wild, confused mental state that high fever can bring on; this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Astrophel, thin, growing wild in sort of green

explanation.surface: A plant called Astrophel, spindly and straggling, in a particular green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing wild' makes NTHI, which 'in' places inside the green. In Spenser's elegy Astrophel, the flower the dead hero becomes is called Penthia by some, Starlight by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Penthia is Spenser's alternative name for the flower astrophel, so the two names denote the same plant.

clue.text: Impressions: odd ones from Renoir — no Paris suite arranged (9, two words)

indicators.note: arranged says those picked letters are put into a new order
the odd ones are the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the following words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd ones from' runs across all four words: RENOIRNOPARISSUITE gives RNINPRSUT, which 'arranged' reorders.
explanation.definitionFit: A print run is the number of copies printed at one go; impressions is the printer's word for such copies.

clue.text: Copper drafted into unit precisely when expected (5, two words)

Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman is posted to his unit right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drafted into' puts the copper inside ONE; 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, by its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor comes in on cue at the moment signalled, so the phrase means at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: Worried re self, little energy within — we'll sound out opinion

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Anxious about oneself and low on energy, a pollster speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns RESELF into FELERS, and 'within' puts E inside it. The definition is spoken by the answer itself: feelers are what 'we' put out to test opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting out feelers means tentatively probing others' views, so feelers are things that test opinion.

clue.text: Fungus wife used as stuffing for chicken? Drink follows (10, two words, apostrophe)

W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
a swig is a gulp of drink

explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer's wig is the shaggy ink cap mushroom, named for its resemblance to a barrister's white wig.

clue.text: Body's cut in salt

indicators.note: in places the word for cut inside the word for salt

parts.note: sal is the Latin and chemists' word for salt, as in sal volatile
to omit something is to cut it out

explanation.surface: A body is chopped up and packed in salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Somital means relating to somites, the segments of an animal's body, so it is an adjective of the body.

clue.text: Bolt spar in Portaloo?

clue.text: Attorney appearing before Congress US dismissed as a brigand

the letters removed

explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is a member of an armed gang of robbers in India or Burma, a bandit.

clue.text: Some filigreed edging supplying wherewithal for thatcher?

explanation.definitionFit: Thatchers work with reeds, so something supplied with them, or covered with them, is reeded.

clue.text: Non-standard spelling out of place in the ABC

clue.text: Teeth on edge? What they'll cause at cutting wages dreadfully (7, two words)

dreadfully says the letters of wages are thrown out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder

clue.text: Charge for coat dress taken up over leg

clue.text: Failed to experience the dawn? We ——, though blotto!

clue.text: Being wary about wicket reduced score
